jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow Systems Engineering–Early systems integration in AI-enabled systems-of-systems
jobs.description:
Do you want to contribute to the development of knowledge, insight and solutions that are relevant to society and working life today and in the future?
We are looking for a PhD research fellow within Systems Engineering.

Why do companies still end up doing engineering on site during commissioning – even when they have built most of the systems themselves? Find the root causes and change how complex systems come together. 
About the position
Do you want to change how complex systems come together – so that integration happens early, not during commissioning? Join us as a PhD research fellow at the Department of Science and Industry Systems, campus Kongsberg. Start: May 2027 (at the latest August 2027).

You will be part of SFI CELECT – the Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems – whose vision is to do more with less, and faster. The centre, funded by the Research Council of Norway, brings together Norway's leading industrial companies and 30 PhD candidates across USN, NTNU and the University of Agder. Industrial cases will be selected among CELECT partners such as Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, Kongsberg Maritime, Forsvarsmateriell, the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), Nammo, Knightec Group, Fylkeskommuner (Buskerud, Vestfold, Telemark), Kongsberg kommune, Sirkulære Rjukan, and Herøya industry park and others. You will also join the Industrial Research School in Complex Systems (INRESCOS).

The position is a three-year educational position with pure organised research training. A four-year appointment with 25 % career-advancing work may be considered.

You must apply for and be admitted to the doctoral programme in Technology (Systems Engineering) within three months of starting. The programme includes courses of about six months (30 ECTS), an independent thesis, research dissemination, a trial lecture and a public defence.

Your workplace will be shared between campus Kongsberg and one or several CELECT partner companies. Depending on the project, you will spend between 3 and 30 months located at the company's premises. You are expected to be present at campus or at the company during ordinary working hours.

Campus Kongsberg sits at the heart of one of Norway's strongest technology clusters, with world-leading companies in maritime, defence, aerospace, energy and subsea technology. Research and industry work side by side – giving you a unique network and strong career opportunities in industry or academia.
About the doctoral project
The aim of this PhD is to develop a methodology that moves systems integration to an earlier stage of the life cycle, by addressing its organisational, human and technical root causes.

Modern products are part of systems-of-systems that must work together for decades. Integration problems often appear only during commissioning – but their root causes lie much earlier: in how organisations, people and technology interact, and in promises made already in the sales phase.

Questions you could explore:

• What are the root causes of late integration problems?
• How can engineering management be involved early – including in sales – and how do you convince an organisation to do it?
You will help shape the final research questions together with your supervisors and industry partners.

The project is part of SFI CELECT (project PhD1.5), headed by Kristin FalkUsing industry as your laboratory, you will work alongside engineers and systems architects on real development projects. A research stay abroad, for example at TNO-ESI in the Netherlands or DTU in Denmark, may be possible.

The projectfocuses on integration across systems and organisations, and complements positions on early design and validation (PhD1.3), life-cycle management of long-living systems (PhD1.4) and competence development for industry (PhD5.1).

Duties

• Complete the doctoral programme up to completion of the doctoral degree within the employment period
• Conduct high-calibre research within the framework described above
• Academic publications in high-quality journals and conferences
• Actively work with companies in an industry-as-laboratory environment, combining qualitative and quantitative research
• Report progress and deliver outputs to the CELECT centre
• Participate in the Norwegian Industrial Systems Engineering Research Group (NISE)
• Active involvement in SFI CELECT's doctoral team across NTNU, USN and UiA, including the research school INRESCOS, and participation in common workshops, learning events and courses
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign research and educational institutions
• Be prepared for changes in your work tasks after appointmentQualifications
All items are requirements, unless it is specified that they are preferred qualifications.  

• Master's degree (120 ECTS credits) within Systems Engineering, Systems Architecture, mechanical, electrical or software engineering, cybernetics, industrial economics and technology management or a similar relevant engineering discipline
• Documented knowledge of relevant methodologies, both quantitative and/or qualitative, at master's level
• Weighted average grade of B or higher on the master's degree and thesis
• The master’s thesis must have been submitted for assessment by the application deadline for the position and approved before starting in the position
• Knowledge of systems integration, systems-of-systems engineering, interface management or MBSE is preferred
• Industrial experience from integration, commissioning, project engineering or sales of complex systems, preferably from Norwegian industry, is preferred
• Understanding of and interest in AI and digital engineering is preferred
• Experience with qualitative research methods (interviews, case studies) is preferred
• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language, or Norwegian at level B2, is preferred
• Excellent written and oral English language skills
• Meet the formal requirements for admission to USN's doctoral programmes and the Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences' doctoral programme in Technology, with the topic of Systems Engineering, no later than three months after starting in the position.
 

Personal qualities

In order to be able to complete a doctoral degree, you need to be able to:

• demonstrate motivation and potential for research in the field
• work independently, but also participate in teamwork
•  work in a structured way, set goals, and make plans to achieve them
•  present and discuss your research with other academics
• get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity
• show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject area
• analyse data, assess different perspectives, and draw well-founded conclusions
• work collaboratively in an industrial setting with the CELECT partners
• be flexible and open to adjusting the project plan as necessary
• have the academic skills and personal qualities to be able to complete the doctoral programme within the employment period
When assessing applications, particular importance will be attached to

• Formal qualifications
• The personal qualities mentioned above
• Motivation letter
• Work experience from Norwegian industry
• Qualifications and experience in systems integration, systems-of-systems engineering or closely related fieldsRequirements for proficiency in English 
This position requires good English language skills. International applicants must document this with a valid certificate from one of the following tests. Specific requirements regarding grades can be found on our webpage English requirement for programmes and subjects taught in English at USN.

• TOEFL – Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT)
• IELTS – International English Language Testing Service

The following applicants are exempt from the requirements listed above:

Applicants from Norway can confirm their English language skills by submitting their upper secondary school diploma.
Requirements for proficiency in Norwegian
The position has no formal requirement for proficiency in Norwegian. Proficiency in a Scandinavian language, or Norwegian at level B2 (language levels as defined by HK-dir.), is preferred.

Applicants who wish this to be taken into account must document their language skills in the application (see How to apply).
Requirements regarding a licence and/or security clearance
The applicant must meet the requirements for authorization for restricted. You can read more about security clearance on the websites of the National Security Authority and the Civil Clearance Authority. 

For the position, an export licence is also required, and the applicant must meet the requirements for this. You can read more about export licences on DEKSA's website.
Motivation letter
Applicants must submit a motivation letter with the application. This should be short and concise, maximum 500 words.

The final project description and work plan will be prepared in consultation with the supervisor(s) during the first three months of the employment period. It is a prerequisite that you complete the project during the employment period.
What we offer
• Organised research training in a large undertaking with an important social mission
• Careers advice and guidance throughout the entire doctoral programme. Together we will draw up a career plan that includes the skills and knowledge you will acquire
• An inclusive working environment with ambitious colleagues
• The opportunity to take Norwegian language courses
• Salary in accordance with the Norwegian State salary scale for PhD research fellows (position code 1017) NOK 550,800. In special cases, code 1378 may be used. Any further increases in pay grade will be based on length of service in the position
• Deductions will be made from your salary in order to make statutory contributions to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund on your behalf
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, ensuring favourable pension, insurance and loan schemesDiversity
We believe that diversity is a resource in our work and learning environment. Different experiences and backgrounds contribute to different perspectives and better solutions to challenges that need to be solved.

We are committed to respecting each other's differences and will facilitate employees with disabilities. We take into account your needs and your situation in different phases of life.

If you find this position interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, disability, cultural background or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, gaps in their CV or an immigrant background, we will call at least one applicant in each of these groups for an interview. If you recognize yourself in one of these categories, you can tick the box in our job search portal.

The university aims to recruit more women to PhD positions within the field. If multiple applicants are considered to have equivalent qualifications, a woman will be given priority over a man.
General information
The Appointment Committee for Fellowship Positions (TUS) is the appointing authority for this position. Your competence for the position will be assessed by an expert committee. The expert committee will assess your competence for the position based on the documentation you have registered in Jobbnorge. 

Based on the expert committee’s assessment, relevant applicants will be invited to an interview and to hold a trial lecture. References will also be obtained for relevant candidates. 

Employment at USN is carried out in accordance with the principles set out in the Norwegian Civil Service Act, and the legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services. If your application is considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter legislation, it will be rejected without further consideration.

The University's Guidelines for Recruitment Positions provide a more detailed description of the criteria for appointment as a PhD research fellow.

As an employee of USN, you must at all times adapt to changes in the field and all organisational changes that are adopted.
How to apply
If you think this position looks interesting and matches your qualifications, you can submit an application electronically by clicking on “Apply for the position” on this page. Here you will need to enter a short application text and information about your relevant education and work experience. In the application text, you must clearly describe your skills and motivation for the position. 

The application must include:

jobs.description:

Want to work on the data and business logic at the centre of a growing software platform? Your Headway is looking for a Software Engineer on behalf of a client in the hospitality technology sector.

Our client builds cloud-based tools that help hospitality businesses run their day-to-day operations. Its platform brings together capabilities such as sales, booking, reporting and integrations, and the company is growing across several Nordic countries.

• Ownership of systems at the heart of a growing Nordic platform.

The position is based in Oslo. Much of the team is in Stavanger, and Oslo-based employees travel there at least once a month, with somewhat more travel during onboarding.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Science and Technology Studies (STS)
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Interdisciplinary Studies of Culture (KULT) is a leading Norwegian centre in (amongst others) the field of Science and Technology Studies (STS). The department falls under the Faculty of Humanities of the Norwegian University of Science and Technology NTNU and is located in Trondheim, Norway. We are currently recruiting a PhD Research Fellow in STS who wants to work at the crossroads of infrastructures, security, resilience, and interdisciplinary work across these fields. 

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD research fellow, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a range of leading positions in higher education and research as well as business and administration. 

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. You will have a daily supervisor at the department, and one or more co-supervisors from across the project team. 
About the project
How do we build a society that is resilient to crises, attacks, and unexpected shocks? A More Resilient Society is a major strategic initiative at NTNU that requires interdisciplinarity and innovative thinking to address complex and socially relevant challenges. A total of 16 PhD candidates will work across faculties and academic communities within the fields of critical societal infrastructure and health preparedness. The aim is to support research that challenges established assumptions and contributes to a safer and more resilient society.  

STRIDE (Synergizing Transport Resilience, Infrastructure, and Defense in Extremes) is one of the projects under the More Resilient Society initiative. STRIDE is a multidisciplinary research project developing a dynamic, multi-risk modeling framework to enhance the resilience of Norway's transport infrastructure against converging climate-driven hazards, such as severe floods and landslides, and geopolitical threats, including targeted sabotage. Moving beyond traditional, brittle "fail-safe" design paradigms, STRIDE operationalizes a "safe-to-fail" approach focused on maintaining critical transport functionality through graceful degradation and rapid recovery across the entire disaster management cycle. As a PhD candidate, you will work within a collaborative, cross-faculty team spanning civil engineering, artificial intelligence, operations research, and science and technology studies.

You will focus on integration of knowledge across academic domains, the operationalization of concepts such as ‘comprehensive resilience’ (Norwegian: totalberedskap) in a multidisciplinary context, and the sociotechnical analysis of infrastructures and their vulnerabilities. 
Duties of the position
You will be offered a position for 4 years as a paid PhD Research Fellow (stipendiat). This will consist of 2,5 years independent research, 0,5 year of courses at PhD level, and 1 year of career-relevant work which may or may not include teaching. More specifically, your duties will be to:

• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out high-quality research within the framework described above
• Produce academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in several research groups at KULT, notably the newly established group on Security Studies (and the related university-wide research group on Security Narratives), and the longstanding Center for Climate, Energy and the Environment (CLEEN).
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching (dependent on the Department’s needs and opportunities)
• Other career-promoting work, such as project support and assistance in grant acquisition.
Changes to your work duties may occur after employment, and flexibility is appreciated.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Doctoral Programme in Interdisciplinary Studies of Culture (PHKULT, https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phkult), see also Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a Master's degree in a relevant subject area. Relevant areas include: Science and Technology Studies (STS), fields such as philosophy, history, sociology and anthropology with a distinctly technology-oriented focus, innovation studies and innovation management, and history and philosophy of science (HPS). Within these fields, it is crucial that you demonstrate an affinity with and aptitude for qualitative and interpretive research. We will also consider candidates from the natural and engineering sciences, provided that they can demonstrate affinity and aptitude for humanities and social sciences. 
• Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than August 2027. Documentation needs to be provided with the application, certifying that this is a realistic expectation (e.g. letter from supervisor). 
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent command of the English language, both written and orally.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.

In order to secure a good fit with the project, candidates are strongly recommended to seek informal contact with the envisioned daily supervisor, Govert Valkenburg (see below), in good time before submitting the application, to acquire more detailed information about the project. 
Preferred selection criteria
• Demonstrable interdisciplinary experience, either within the humanities and social sciences (HSS), or even outside HSS, with fields like engineering, natural science or medical science.
• Demonstrable collaborative research experience, including possible internships.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian. If this is not the case, willingness to learn will be considered an advantage. Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues

• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)

As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work in addition to 1 year of career promotion work. 

The successful candidate will be granted conditional admission to the PHKULT doctoral programme when employed in the PhD research fellow position. It is a prerequisite for continued employment that the requirements for full admission are met within three months, and that you continue to participate in the organized doctoral programme for the remainder of the employment period. For more information about the requirements for full admission, please see Section 6 of the PhD regulations. 

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. If you are invited for an interview, you must present certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

• CV filled out in Jobbnorge
• Copy of Master's thesis. If the thesis is not in English or a Scandinavian language, add an extended summary in English or Norwegian. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline proposing your approach to the project in terms of research questions, theoretical perspectives and methodological design, as well as a tentativeprogress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages).
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Any publications or other relevant research work
• Any relevant certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts of, your education has been taken outside Norway, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution does not offer a “diploma supplement”, you must attach information about the grading scale from the education institution. 

We further recommend that you enclose a statement about your education abroad from the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir). Follow the link to their web site for more information about how to obtain such a statement: Apply for recognition of foreign higher education. See also NTNU’s web site for documentation requirements for education obtained outside Norway. 

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

About the role
Want to build and ship AI systems that professionals rely on for real work? Crunched is looking for a senior engineer who wants to own the hard problems from architecture to production – in a small team moving fast.
About Crunched
Crunched builds an autonomous AI analyst for strategy, finance and advisory workflows, bringing AI agents into Excel rather than asking users to change how they work. The company is backed by Y Combinator and has raised NOK 55 million in seed funding.

The engineering challenge goes beyond a chatbot: agents, data flows and reliable execution need to work together in a product used for consequential decisions. You will work close to the founders, customers and engineers, with room to shape the stack and engineering culture. This is a high-intensity, on-site role in Oslo – a fit for someone who values ownership and building together in person.
What you will do
• Build and ship autonomous AI workflows used by professional customers
• Work across Python, TypeScript, React, Postgres, FastAPI and LangGraph
• Own features from architecture and implementation to production operation
• Improve reliability, evaluation, observability and user experienceWho we are looking for
• Strong professional experience building and shipping software
• Strong backend or full-stack engineering fundamentals
• Experience shipping production systems with high ownership
• Practical interest in LLMs, agents and reliable AI systems
• Comfortable working five days on-site in OsloWhat we offer
• High ownership in a small and ambitious engineering team
• Direct customer impact and short decision paths
• Competitive compensation benchmarked against leading technology companies

The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (IBM) has a vacancy for a PhD Candidate on Impacts of Interdependent Multi-Hazards on Transport Systems (four-year position).

As part of the interdisciplinary STRIDE initiative, this PhD project addresses the critical challenge of how converging climate-driven multi-hazards, such as intense storms, floods, and water-induced landslides, interact with acute security threats like targeted sabotage across transport networks.

Current hazard assessments remain largely siloed and static, failing to capture the non-linear, compounding feedback loops that occur when natural risks and human intelligence threats overlap. In STRIDE you will develop a hybrid multi-hazard framework that bridges physics-based simulations with data-driven statistical and machine learning approaches. Your work will pioneer spatiotemporal fragility functions to quantify how multi-hazard disruptions propagate along critical transport corridors.

This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

We invite applications for a PhD Candidate position focused on modelling risk and vulnerability in the supply chains for drone detection and interception systems. The position is based at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management, located at NTNU’s campus in Trondheim.

The mission of Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management is to carry out education and research activities at a high international level in the intersection between technology/natural sciences and business economics, management, and HSE to promote sustainable value creation in technology-based areas in industry, business, and public sector organizations in Norway.
About the position
A more resilient society is increasingly dependent on robust critical infrastructure across different sectors. The geopolitical situation in Europe, including experiences from war and hybrid threats, shows that critical infrastructure can be deliberately targeted using low-cost, commercially available technology, especially drones. There is a need for knowledge and solutions on how to prevent damage to critical infrastructure caused by drone attacks. The threat landscape, technological development, and resilience capabilities are changing rapidly. This increases the demand for research-based innovation and rapid adaptation.

Protecting critical infrastructure against drone attacks depends not only on effective technologies. This PhD position focuses on the supply chains for drone detection and interception systems where the project aims to generate knowledge about risks and vulnerabilities in supply chains associated with the development, production, procurement, deployment, and operation of drone technologies used to counter drone threats to critical infrastructure. Experiences from the war in Ukraine have highlighted significant vulnerabilities in the supply chains underpinning drone detection and interception capabilities. Effective counter-drone systems depend not on a single technology, but on complex and interconnected ecosystems comprising industrial systems, sensors, software, communication networks, skilled operators, interceptor technologies and logistics. The project will push the research frontier by developing methods and models for assessing risk and vulnerability across end-to-end supply chains that support the development and operation of drone-based detection and interception capabilities.

The PhD candidate will:

• Investigate and model how dependencies (suppliers, critical components, data, infrastructure, logistics, market conditions, and regulations) and mechanisms create vulnerabilities in national and international supply chains. 
• Develop dynamic risk and vulnerability models for drone-related supply chains using AI-supported analytical methods that integrate historical and real-time data from both civilian and military domains. 
• Demonstrate how such models can support risk-informed decision-making at tactical, operational, and strategic levels in supply chains.Research environment
The position is part of the project ‘Managing drone threats to critical infrastructure’. The primary objective of the research project is to contribute to a more resilient society by developing knowledge and solutions to understand, manage, and respond to drone threats and attacks against critical infrastructure. The research project will develop and integrate technological, organizational and supply-chain knowledge needed to contribute to robustness and resilience for Norwegian critical infrastructure against rapidly evolving drone threats, thereby strengthening societal resilience, national preparedness and scientific understanding of hybrid risks.

The project consists of four PhD projects:

• Drone detection and interception. Objective: develop solutions for drone detection & interception for protection of critical infrastructure
• Consequences of drone attacks. Objective: test and simulate detonating drones and their impacts on critical infrastructures
• Modelling risk and vulnerability in the supply chains for drone detection and interception systems. Objective: develop knowledge on risks and vulnerabilities in value chains for protecting against drone threats to critical infrastructures (this position)
• Organizing and decision-making in drone operations. Objective: develop organization models and decision-making frameworks for drone operations
The four PhD projects are hosted by the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management, the Department of Engineering Cybernetics and the Department of Structural Engineering. The research project is thus multidisciplinary. All project members will contribute to added scientific value across the work packages. The project will thus be organized to ensure multidisciplinary research through e.g. joint scenarios to be addressed across the PhD projects, joint publications across the PhD projects and frequent meetings. There are clear input-output relations between the four PhD projects that will strengthen the multidisciplinary added value.

Transport systems can be disrupted by events such as floods, landslides, traffic accidents, and technical failures. These disruptions can close or constrain links in the transport network, affecting the movement of passengers and goods.

This PhD project will develop optimization methods to support strategic and operational decisions in multimodal transport systems. Strategic decisions may include infrastructure investments, resource placement, and infrastructure reinforcement. Operational decisions may include rerouting traffic, allocating capacity, and planning recovery.

You will work closely with another PhD candidate who is developing dynamic transport models and machine-learning methods to predict how the network performs under different conditions. You will integrate these models into optimization methods, allowing, for example, many scenarios and resilience measures to be evaluated efficiently.

The project addresses research questions like:

• How can optimization support strategic investment and resource-allocation decisions for resilient transport systems?
• How can dynamic transport models and machine-learning methods improve optimization across many possible scenarios?
• How can optimization support rerouting, capacity allocation, and recovery decisions when parts of a transport system are unavailable?
The PhD candidate will develop models for strategic resilience planning and operational disruption management. The research will examine how to balance efficiency, redundancy, recovery, and societal requirements.

Use cases will be developed in close collaboration with project partners, including Norway’s railway infrastructure manager (Bane NOR), the Norwegian Public Roads Administration (Statens vegvesen), and the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI). The candidate will work with partners to examine practical decisions related to transport resilience.

The position offers an opportunity to develop optimization methods for important decisions about transport resilience, in collaboration with researchers in optimization, machine learning, transport modelling, infrastructure, and social sciences.
Research environment
The PhD position is part of STRIDE: Synergizing Transport Resilience, Infrastructure, and Defense in Extremes, an interdisciplinary research project involving researchers in transport modelling, machine learning, optimization, infrastructure, and social sciences.

The project studies how transport systems respond to disruptions and how modelling and decision-support methods can strengthen resilience across planning, response, and recovery. The PhD candidate will work closely with three other PhD candidates studying interdependent hazards, data-driven modelling of multimodal transport, and the societal dimensions of resilience and total defense.

The PhD candidate will be hosted at the Managerial Economics, Finance and Operations Research (BEDØK) group at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management. The EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet is currently being deployed, with the intention to provide citizens with easier and expanded access to public and private services. Digital identity wallets will potentially become a critical socio-technical infrastructure also in Norway, and raises challenges related to issues such as privacy, fairness, stakeholder engagement and securityi. On this background the project's overall goal is to develop knowledge, methodologies and competencies that strengthen Norway's ability to deploy and maintain secure, privacy-preserving and democratically aligned digital identity wallets. Truly interdisciplinary, the challenges cut across issues of digital sovereignty, identity management, security technologies, and sociotechnical practices and imaginaries. Having our critical, digital infrastructures dependent on Big Tech make them vulnerable hence undermines our digital sovereignty. Forecasting models are usually trained on data from normal operating conditions. Project description
A PhD position is available at the Section for Theoretical Chemistry, Department of Chemistry, University of Oslo, within the project Molecular Atmospheric Chemistry on Alien Worlds (MACAW), funded by the Research Council of Norway.In this project we will employ quantum chemistry methods using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to study chemical reactions, photochemistry, identify spectral signatures for potential detection and elucidate condensation mechanisms for molecules in atmospheres beyond that of contemporary Earth. The project has a particular focus on Sulfur and Chlorine chemistry as well as isotopic fractionation processes.The successful applicant will have freedom to pursue specific research topics within the relatively wide project framework, in coordination with the supervisor. The work is first and foremost computational utilizing electronic structure methods to qualitatively study photochemical and thermal reaction mechanisms, as well as quantify reaction rates, UV-Vis spectra and other molecular properties relevant to studying the role of molecules in planetary atmospheres.
